title: Fantastic Health Tracker…but with issues.
text:
I purchased this app many years ago and only recently got the subscription, but I’m not sure it’s worth it yet. It’s been great at tracking food and my overall progress since the beginning.

That said, there are problems. It isn’t saving my logged weight, specifically when I update it after I go back and change it because I keyed a wrong digit, it then reverts back to the previously saved weight. It’s also been randomly deleting my previously logged exercises. I don’t have autopilot enabled, it’s just not saving manually logged changes or updates to already entered logs. It appears to change it, but once you “Save” then close the app and come back, poof your logged entries are gone. Furthermore, it seems to notify me my calorie deficit had changed when it shouldn’t, I now have to discard that page every time I look at it so it doesn’t update my daily max calories. All of this has been an issue since the subscription. 

Hopefully this gets fixed because these core features being unreliable is awful and frustrating and I’m failing to see the benefit of the subscription right now.

title: Room for a few Improvements
text: The app is easy to set up and supports GLP-1 use. The app will communicate back and birth with Apple Health. Use of the full functionality of the app is not cheap but worth the money. When you are on a GLP-1 it is more important to track protein than calorie intake and this app makes that simple. There are a few areas that need improvement, the first being that the app will not import any vitamins that you take even if they are logged in Apple Health. The second being that the app will only show suggested menu items for the current week. It really needs to show the current week and the following week so that you can pick up items for the next week while out shopping for that week. The third being that I am a pretty picky eater and I am sure that I am not the only one, it would be amazing if the app gave you the ability during initial set up to go and specify food items that you do not like. From their the app could create week menu suggestions based upon the users likes and dislikes. This simple suggestion cannot be that hard to incorporate. Finally it is to easy to accidentally log your food under the wrong meal because the meal remains open once you have logged food for that meal. If you don’t pay attention and don’t select the next meal it will log everything under the last meal that was logged.

title: Don’t love that I bought this app and don’t get all the features

title: I’m disappointed
text:
I’m disappointed with the app’s behavior and monetization design. Even after disabling subscription reminders and premium prompts, the app still constantly suggests features that turn out to be Premium-only after you tap them. This is frustrating and feels misleading.

Premium-only features should either be clearly marked everywhere or fully hidden when the user chooses to disable Premium promotions. I don’t need AI tools, advanced analytics, or any of the extra premium clutter. I just want a clean food diary and recipe tracker without endless upsell attempts.

The food database for Russia is also very poor compared to competitors.

Overall, the experience feels unnecessarily pushy and overcomplicated for users who only need basic calorie and recipe tracking.
